claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'GENERATE statement, XIII-66' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'GENERATE statement, XIII-66' then '  Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300dpi render of PDF page 967 (B-55, index G-I, two columns) against page-967.md. The markdown holds every entry and sub-entry in the PDF's order with the same page references (e.g. GENERATE statement, XIII-66 / Imperative statement, IV-39; Implementor-name, IV-8 with its six sub-entries; continuation lines XIII-3 and XVII-87, A-24, B-47 kept indented). Sub-entries are indented by two spaces exactly as the PDF indents them, so the source text preserves both entry boundaries (one per line) and hierarchy. The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match. The only difference is how a Markdown renderer would reflow bare lines: a presentation/formatting matter, not a content discrepancy, on an informative index page. Per the verification rules (reject differences that are only formatting and do not change meaning), not real.
